description:
A `${t}` inside a raw body in a component body (`
${t}
`) is display text, not a prop interpolation (§4.17, S468 "raw content wins"): the page shows the literal `${t}`, and the prop's markup-shaped value builds no element.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S468 "go on the merge driver, your recs on the rest" item 4 (supersedes, for this case, ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S462 Q21 "I like a.")
rationale:
§4.17 as amended S468: "Inside a `
` / `` body a `${…}` is display text, always — including in a component's `renders` body (§66) and a legacy component body (§15.9): it substitutes no prop, reads no cell, and displays exactly as written (`
${t}
` in a component body shows the five characters `${t}`)." A component prop reaches a raw body only as element CONTENT (children / slot), never through an interpolation. Before S468 this case asserted the S462 Q21 reading (the prop substituted, then encoded). impl#1 still substitutes — carried: g-impl1-component-raw-body-substitutes-prop-s468. The bootstrap (with s468-bootstrap-failopen-gaps' raw-content mode) shows a `renders 
${t} …
` body literally (slice-m4/raw-content.test.js "in a declaration's renders"); this legacy-dialect case is not twinned there (component-const).
